questions.question: You need to search the vault for notes about 'auth flow'. What command do you run, and what two identity flags are always required?
questions.expected: Run node .claude/skills/vault-search/scripts/vault-query.mjs with at least one of --entities/--tags/--terms for the query. --instance-id (the harness instance UUID from .squidsquad/.instance-id, or 'unprovisioned' if absent) and --alias (the caller's own agent alias) are REQUIRED on every call.

questions.question: The engine returns its JSON output. Does it include the full body text of the matched notes? What should you do to read a note's actual content?
questions.expected: No -- the output is metadata-only JSON (results + traversed): paths, tiers, scores, link map, no note bodies. To read a note's actual content, use the Read tool on the note's path yourself.

questions.question: You need to find vault notes about 'deployment'. Is it acceptable to run grep -r 'deployment' .squidsquad/vault/ instead of the engine? Why or why not?
questions.expected: No -- raw grep/glob/Read-scanning the vault folders is banned. The engine is the only sanctioned search path; a grep that finds the right note leaves no impression/used telemetry trail, so the note reads as dead to the maintenance signal and gets pruned. Always use the engine Skill instead.

questions.question: You're running a diagnostic test invocation of the engine that isn't a real consumption event. What flag should you pass, and why?
questions.expected: Pass --no-write. It suppresses telemetry writes for diagnostic/side-effect-free searches (tests, CI, debugging) so telemetry measures only real consumption, not test noise.

questions.question: You try to invoke the engine but node is not available on this machine (or the engine call fails). What should you do?
questions.expected: Degrade honestly per VAULT-ARCH 9.9: state in your receipt line that the engine was unavailable. Never fabricate 'none relevant' and never substitute a manual grep-based search.
